# `http` check

Request a URL and check status, body, JSON fields and latency.

```yaml
checks:
  example:
    type: http
    url: https://api.example.com/health
    expect:
      status: [200]
      json: { "$.status": up }
      latency: { warn: 300ms, fail: 2s }
```

## Keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` **(required)** | string |  | URL to request (http:// or https://). |
| `method` | one of: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS | `GET` | HTTP method. |
| `headers` | map of string |  | Request headers. Use ${VAR} plus 'secrets:' for tokens. |
| `body` | string |  | Request body. |
| `follow_redirects` | bool | `true` | Follow up to 10 redirects. |
| `insecure` | bool | `false` | Skip TLS certificate verification (shown in the report). Avoid. |
| `expect` | mapping |  | What counts as healthy. |
| `expect.status` | list of integer |  | Accepted status codes (default: any 2xx). |
| `expect.body_contains` | string |  | Text the response body must contain. |
| `expect.json` | map of string |  | Fields the JSON body must have: path -> expected value. Paths look like $.status or $.items[0].name. |
| `expect.latency` | {warn, fail} duration |  | Total response time limits. Triggers when the value is above the threshold. |

Every check also accepts the [common keys](../config.md#common-check-keys).

One-liner: `medic check http <url> [--set key=value ...]`
